title: Tanzanian Chickpea Curry
community: Popular in coastal and urban Tanzania
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Tanzanian Chickpea Curry — chickpeas simmered in a Zanzibar spice and tomato sauce with coconut milk. The Indian Ocean trading tradition's legume gift to Tanzania — satisfying, protein-rich, and deeply spiced.
longDesc: Chickpeas arrived on the Tanzanian coast through Indian Ocean trade and have become a beloved part of coastal Tanzanian cooking. The Zanzibar spice treatment gives chickpea curry a depth and fragrance that matches any meat dish.
steps: Heat oil. Cook onions until golden.
Add garlic, ginger, and all spices. Stir 1 minute.
Add tomatoes. Cook 8 minutes until very thick.
Add chickpeas. Stir to coat in the base.
Add coconut milk. Simmer gently 15 minutes.
Mash a few chickpeas against the side of the pan to thicken naturally.
chefTips: Mashing a few chickpeas thickens the sauce — no flour needed.
The Zanzibar spice array is what makes this distinctive.
cookingScience: Chickpeas contain more starch than kidney beans — mashing some releases this starch directly into the sauce, creating natural thickening. The remaining whole chickpeas provide texture contrast.
sustainabilityTips: Chickpeas are nitrogen-fixing — very sustainable protein.
culturalNote: Chickpea curry is Tanzania's Indian Ocean legacy in a bowl — the legume that arrived on Arab and Indian trading dhows now as much a part of Tanzanian coastal cooking as coconut milk itself.
